001: Have you started preparing for next week's presentation yet?
Not at all. I don't know where to start.
You should first decide on a topic, then gather your materials.
I see. What do you think would be a good topic?
A topic related to your major would probably be the easiest to work with.
You're right. Then I'll look into environmental issues.
002: Is your presentation material ready yet?
I'm about halfway there, I think. The slide structure is taking a while.
I struggled with the same thing when I made mine before.
How did you manage to organize it well?
I put the conclusion first, then listed the reasons after that.
That's a good method. I'll try that approach right away.
003: Want to practice the presentation together?
Sure. But my script isn't finished yet.
That's fine. I'll listen at this stage and give you advice.
Thanks. Then, can I get some of your time tomorrow afternoon?
Yeah, I'm free starting at three tomorrow.
That helps a lot. I'll contact you again then.
004: I wonder how many minutes the presentation should be.
According to the teacher's instructions, we were told fifteen minutes each.
Fifteen minutes, huh. That's pretty long. I need to prepare the content thoroughly.
Right. Also, we need to consider time for the Q&A session.
I'll predict what might be asked and prepare answers.
That's important. I'll prepare the same way.
005: How should I design the slides to make them easy to read?
I think you should make the text bigger and use lots of diagrams.
True. If it's all text, it's hard to read.
Also, limiting the colors to about three will make it look cleaner.
I see. I'll keep that in mind. What color background do you think is good?
I think white or light gray is a safe choice.
006: Have you memorized your presentation script yet?
I still can't remember it at all, and I'm feeling anxious.
It's okay. If you practice out loud many times, you'll memorize it.
Even so, the closer the actual day gets, the more nervous I become.
I used to be like that too, but you'll gain confidence with practice.
Thanks. I'll practice three times before bed tonight.
007: Did you have the teacher look at your presentation materials?
Not yet. I made an appointment to show them after class tomorrow.
That's good. Getting the teacher's feedback will really improve the content.
I hope so. I'm scared there will be a lot of things to fix.
Even if there are things to fix, that just means you'll grow that much more.
I'll try to think of it that positively. Thanks.
008: Is there a way to not get nervous during the presentation?
I try to take slow, deep breaths.
Yeah. Also, it helps to convince yourself that you know more than anyone in the audience.
That's a good idea. I think I can speak with confidence.
Exactly. And once you get the first words out, the rest will flow naturally.
009: How should I answer questions after the presentation?
If it's a question you don't know, I think you should honestly say so.
But won't that lower my grade?
It's fine. If you say you'll look into it and answer later, it comes across as sincere.
Yeah. Also, it's important to listen carefully to the whole question.
010: Tomorrow's finally the presentation day. Are you all set?
Yeah, I managed to finish the preparations. Now I just have to wait for the real thing.
That's great. I'm sure it'll go well. I'm rooting for you.
Thanks. Hearing your support gave me a little more confidence.
Go to bed early tonight and get yourself in good shape.
I will. Tomorrow, I'm going to give it my all.
